title: Changelog
text:
Changelog

 1.1.0 - Execution fees and account leverage

All customer fills now pay execution fees; spot fees are deducted from received assets. Added account leverage and rollback-only order/leverage previews, per-execution fee fields, average execution prices and BTC pool-fee reporting. Balance activity omits zero-net reservations/releases. Meadow 1.1 adds padded tabs and accessible notifications.

 1.0.0 — 3 November 2026

Initial public documentation release, audited against the implemented REST routes and models: 41 operations, including retired/disabled routes, with request parameters, authentication, response schemas and examples.

- Documented HMAC Read/Trade keys, JWT sessions, cookie rotation and idempotent financial commands.
- Documented aggregated public depth and SignalR revision invalidation; no individual public-order endpoint.
- Added the explicit counterparty-dependent fee configuration and default five-level derivative quoting.
- Documented real-book liquidity contribution/redemption queues, Earn, loans, DCA and local ERC-20 custody.
- Adopted the shared Meadow branding specification and token release.

The API currently uses unversioned /api routes. Breaking changes must be called out here and coordinated with integration consumers; this documentation release number does not introduce a /v1 URL prefix.

title: Build on Novčić
text:
Build on Novčić

div className="guide-hero"
  pConnect market data, manage orders, and integrate account workflows with the Novčić exchange./p
  pStart with the authentication model and exact decimal formats, then explore the endpoint reference for the operation you need./p
/div

div className="guide-links"
  a href="./guides/quickstart/"Make your first request →/a
  a href="./guides/authentication/"Authenticate your integration →/a
  a href="./reference/public/market/"Read aggregated market depth →/a
  a href="./openapi.json"Download OpenAPI 3.0 →/a
/div

 Connection details

| Interface | Address | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Local REST | http://127.0.0.1:8081/api | Public data and authenticated account operations |
| Local SignalR hub | http://127.0.0.1:8081/hubs/market | Revision notifications; fetch snapshots through REST |
| Public documentation | https://novcic.github.io/docs/ | Integration contract and examples |

Set the exchange origin with NOVCIC_URL. A hosted production API origin is not configured or announced in this release. GitHub Pages hosts documentation only; it does not accept trading requests. Network and token contract details come from GET /api/network.

 Choose the correct credentials

Public market data needs no credentials. Automated read access uses a Read API key; automated order placement and cancellation uses a Trade key. Both use HMAC-SHA256 signatures. Browser account management, wallet transfers, withdrawals, product subscriptions and key management use a JWT session. A Trade key does not grant withdrawal or transfer access.

Novčić uses its own routes, signature payload and response shapes. Familiar navigation patterns are informed by [Bybit's integration documentation](https://bybit-exchange.github.io/docs/v5/guide); this API is not wire-compatible with Bybit.

 Integration essentials

- Keep amounts and prices as decimal strings. Use decimal arithmetic, never binary floating point for balances or order sizing.
- Discover instruments through /api/products. Submit their canonical id, including BTC-PERP for the perpetual whose display symbol is BTCUSDT.
- Persist an Idempotency-Key UUID for each financial intent. A retry uses the same key and body, with a new HMAC nonce and timestamp.
- A successful order submission can be partially filled or cancelled. Check the returned state and reconcile executions.
- SignalR announces invalidations, not order-book deltas. Refresh snapshots on connection and reconnection.
- History endpoints return bounded recent lists without pagination. Persist the execution and ledger data your application needs.

The [changelog](./changelog.md) records contract changes. [Maintenance](./maintenance.md) describes how the separate documentation repository stays synchronized with the exchange.

title: Authentication
text:
Authentication

 Permissions

| Credential | Read account data | Orders, previews, leverage | Transfers, custody writes, Earn, LP, DCA | Manage keys |
|  | --- | --- | --- |
| Public | Public routes only | No | No | No |
| Read HMAC key | Yes | No | No | No |
| Trade HMAC key | Yes | Yes | No | No |
| JWT session | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |

Create keys through the exchange API access page or POST /api/keys with a JWT session. Names are limited to 60 characters. At most ten active, unexpired keys are allowed per account. Keys expire after 90 days. The secret is returned only at creation; list responses contain metadata only. Revoking a key prevents subsequent authentication.

 HMAC headers

| Header | Value |
| --- | --- |
| X-Api-Key | Key UUID returned at creation |
| X-Api-Timestamp | UTC Unix time in milliseconds as decimal text |
| X-Api-Nonce | Fresh UUID per HTTP attempt |
| X-Api-Signature | Hex-encoded HMAC-SHA256 digest |
| Idempotency-Key | Stable command UUID on financial POSTs |
| Content-Type | application/json when sending a JSON body |

The timestamp must be within 30 seconds of server time in either direction. Synchronize your host clock. Nonces cannot be replayed within their validity window, even if the signature is otherwise correct.

Construct exactly six lines, joined with LF (\n), with no additional trailing newline:

text
timestamp
nonce
UPPERCASE_HTTP_METHOD
/api/path?raw=query
idempotency-key-or-empty
exact-request-body-or-empty


The path includes the original query string in its transmitted order and encoding, but excludes origin and fragment. Serialize JSON once and sign the same UTF-8 bytes you send. Whitespace, property order, escaping and query ordering matter to signatures. GET normally has an empty fifth and sixth line.

Use the returned secret string as UTF-8 text. Do not hex-decode it before using it as the HMAC key. The secret looks hexadecimal, but the server signs with its literal UTF-8 representation.

javascript
import {createHmac, randomUUID} from 'node:crypto';
const timestamp = Date.now().toString();
const nonce = randomUUID();
const method = 'GET', path = '/api/balances', body = '', commandKey = '';
const canonical = [timestamp, nonce, method, path, commandKey, body].join('\n');
const signature = createHmac('sha256', process.env.NOVCIC_SECRET)
  .update(canonical, 'utf8').digest('hex');


Complete runnable [JavaScript](https://github.com/novcic/docs/blob/master/examples/signed-request.mjs) and [Python](https://github.com/novcic/docs/blob/master/examples/signed_request.py) examples include response handling and deterministic test vectors. Keep keys in server-side environment variables; never embed them in browser bundles or documentation URLs.

 JWT sessions

Register or log in to receive accessToken, expiresAt, and a minimal user. Send Authorization: Bearer accessToken for private requests. Access tokens last ten minutes. Login and registration also set the HttpOnly novcic_refresh cookie, scoped to /api/auth, with SameSite Strict and a seven-day lifetime. Secure-cookie behavior is deployment-configured; deployed HTTPS environments should enable it.

POST /api/auth/refresh rotates the refresh token. Serialize refresh calls: replaying an already-used refresh token revokes the whole session family. Logout revokes that family and clears the cookie; an already-issued access JWT remains valid until expiry. Non-browser clients must maintain a cookie jar for session refresh.

Send same-origin requests from the exchange browser application. Cross-origin POSTs with a mismatched Origin authority are rejected. The documentation site does not collect or store credentials, and there is no browser trading console in these docs.

 Diagnose authentication failures

For 401, check key expiry/revocation, scope, clock skew, nonce reuse, path encoding, exact body, and secret encoding. Some 401 responses have no JSON body. Public routes do not require signed headers. /api/keys explicitly requires JWT even when the operation is GET.

title: Deposits and withdrawals
text:
Deposits and withdrawals

The configured custody network is a local Ethereum chain, ID 31337, with ERC-20 BTC (8 decimals) and USDT (6 decimals). Read /api/network for the current contract addresses, chain generation and confirmation requirement. No native Bitcoin deposit address or mainnet deposit network is implemented.

 Deposit

1. Authenticate with a JWT session and POST {} to /api/custody/address.
2. Query /api/network; use the current token contract and matching local chain.
3. Send the supported ERC-20 token to the returned address from your wallet.
4. Poll /api/custody/history and /api/balances.

The address is stable for an account. Deposit discovery reads ERC-20 Transfer logs; confirmations are checked against canonical block hashes. A deposit normally progresses Pending → Confirmed → Credited. The configured requirement is three confirmations. The balance credit lands in Funding exactly once. Duplicate log processing and credit retries cannot mint another balance credit.

Custody may sweep deposits after crediting. Sweeps and gas-management jobs are internal and do not appear as customer withdrawals. Reorganizations or a changed chain generation can pause/quarantine processing; read status/error and avoid assuming a timeout means a lost transfer.

 Withdraw

POST /api/withdraw requires a JWT, an idempotency key, supported asset, positive amount and nonzero Ethereum address. Funds must be in Funding. The command moves available funds into locked withdrawal reserves, then returns the queued transfer.

Normal lifecycle: Requested → Signed → Broadcast → Confirmed → Completed. A definitive reverted receipt produces Reverted → Failed and releases the reserved funds. An ambiguous broadcast or RPC failure remains pending for reconciliation; funds are not refunded merely because a response timed out. The same signed transaction can be rebroadcast safely.

Use /api/custody/history for current status and transaction hash. Request receipts contain the initial state and do not update when the chain transaction progresses. Signed API keys cannot request withdrawals. There is no public withdrawal-cancel, address-whitelist, arbitrary-chain or native-ETH transfer endpoint.

 Local provisioning

The exchange repository owns chain/setup.mjs and the local deployment scripts. Re-running normal bootstrap reuses the existing chain deployment when valid; deliberate chain resets require the documented reset workflow and a new generation. Token addresses are deployment data, not constants to copy from a documentation example. Never point these local-chain tokens or addresses at an unrelated network.

title: Recurring BTC purchases
text:
Recurring BTC purchases

POST /api/dca creates a recurring spot BTC purchase using Unified Trading USDT. Supply amount in USDT per run, hours as 1/24/168, and an optional total budget. Amount supports six decimals; budget must cover at least one run.

The first run is scheduled one interval in the future. Creating a plan does not reserve its future budget. The execution worker uses the real spot book; it cannot buy without available funds and counterparties. A run can fill partially or record a skipped/failure outcome. The schedule tracks actual spent value and its latest human-readable lastOutcome.

Read /api/portfolio.schedules for nextRun, paused state, spent, budget and outcome. Budget is a cumulative cap, not a wallet allocation. Keep sufficient trading funds available while accounting for concurrent orders and margin requirements.

POST /api/toggle-dca toggles pause/resume for a schedule ID. Resume schedules the next attempt one interval from now. Persist the idempotency key: a retry with a new key could toggle the schedule back. There is no update/delete endpoint or catch-up promise for every missed interval.

title: Errors and limits
text:
Errors and limits

Responses use ordinary HTTP status codes. There is no Bybit-style retCode envelope and no stable numeric application error taxonomy. Domain errors usually contain {"error":"Human-readable reason"}. Treat the message as display text, not a machine-readable enum.

| Status | Meaning | Recovery |
|  | --- |
| 200 | Request processed; inspect resource status | Reconcile fills, queues or settlement separately |
| 400 | Invalid input, precision, insufficient funds/collateral, stale reference or idempotency conflict | Inspect error and current state before a corrected intent |
| 401 | Missing/invalid/expired credentials, signature or scope | Reauthenticate or correct signing; body may be empty |
| 403 | POST Origin authority mismatch | Use same-origin session requests or a server integration |
| 404 | Unknown route/resource routing, or disabled faucet | Check path and deployment capabilities |
| 410 | Retired standalone liquidity/swap route | Use queued liquidity or ordinary spot orders |
| 429 | Authentication rate limit exceeded | Back off; body may be empty |
| 5xx / timeout | Service/downstream failure or ambiguous network result | Retry financial commands with the same command key |

Domain “not found” conditions can return 400 rather than 404. ASP.NET request-binding errors may use a framework response instead of the domain error shape. Always inspect status and content type before parsing JSON, and tolerate an empty error body.

 Current limits

- Register, login and refresh share a fixed window of 30 requests per minute per remote IP. There are no published per-key trading quotas or rate-limit response headers in this implementation.
- API proxy POST bodies are limited to 8,192 bytes when content length is known; signed requests also enforce the limit after reading the body. Keep payloads small.
- HMAC timestamps have a ±30-second window. Each attempt needs a new nonce.
- Maximum ten active unexpired keys; keys expire after 90 days.
- Orders and executions: latest 200 each. Ledger and custody history: latest 100 each. Portfolio risk events and LP requests: latest 100 each.
- Candles: up to 500 buckets. There are no cursor/offset history parameters.

Do not assume an absent explicit trading quota means unlimited capacity. Coalesce market refreshes, use bounded request concurrency and exponential backoff with jitter. No rate-limit headers, retry-after promise, bulk order endpoint, private event stream or historical export endpoint is currently part of the public contract.

title: Execution fees
text:
Execution fees

Read /api/config for configured rates. feeModel is execution. Both customer makers and takers pay on every fill, including customer-to-customer executions. Unfilled quantity pays no fee.

| Product | Default rate | Fee asset |
|  | --- |
| Spot buy | Received BTC × 0.001 (0.10%) | BTC, deducted from receipt |
| Spot sell | Received USDT × 0.001 (0.10%) | USDT, deducted from receipt |
| Perpetual / expiry futures | Executed notional × 0.00055 (0.055%) | USDT |
| Options | min(quantity × index × 0.0003, premium notional × 0.07) | USDT |

On a customer fill against the AMM, 80% of the fee goes to the pool in the same asset and 20% to the exchange. Customer-to-customer fees go entirely to the exchange. Internal AMM, conversion and liquidation accounts are exempt from customer fees. Pool BTC and USDT fees are reported separately as feesEarnedBtc and feesEarned; both are already included in NAV.

Fees round down to eight decimal places per fill. The pool share rounds down again; the exchange receives the remainder. Settlement, fees and allocations commit atomically with the order receipt.

For example, buying 0.001 BTC at 75,000 USDT spends 75 USDT and receives 0.000999 BTC after a 0.000001 BTC fee. If the seller is the AMM, the pool receives 0.00000080 BTC and the exchange 0.00000020 BTC. An ordinary customer seller instead pays 0.075 USDT from their sale proceeds.

Private execution responses include buyerFee, sellerFee, buyerFeeAsset, and sellerFeeAsset. Historical executions predating these fields return null; use their historical ledger entries for reconciliation. Average execution price excludes fees. Wallet activity calls fees Execution fee; older raw entries can retain AMM execution fee.

Use POST /api/order-preview for maximum quantity and estimates. Spot Max does not reserve an extra input-asset fee. Derivative sizing includes fees and collateral obligations, and resting derivative orders reserve fee capacity. A preview is a snapshot, not a promise: submission rechecks prices, balances and margin atomically.

title: Earn and collateralized loans
text:
Earn and collateralized loans

Earn subscriptions and loans use Unified Trading balances and JWT session authentication. All commands require stable idempotency keys. Read public lending-pool state from /api/products and account holdings from /api/portfolio.

 Earn shares

POST /api/supply accepts asset and token amount. It accrues interest first, transfers funds to pool cash and issues proportional shares. Pool unit value is (cash + debt − reserves) / shares; the initial unit is one token per share. A share balance is not necessarily the current redeemable token amount.

POST /api/redeem accepts the same request shape, but amount means shares. It increases queuedShares. The queue pays as pool cash becomes available, updating shares and queued shares together. Lending utilization can prevent immediate full redemption. Pending shares remain part of the holding until payment. There is no guaranteed liquidity or fixed advertised yield.

 Borrowing

POST /api/borrow borrows BTC against USDT or USDT against BTC. The two assets must differ. Initial LTV is capped at 60%, using a fresh index, and the lending pool must have available cash. Collateral moves out of available Unified Trading funds into loan collateral accounting.

The annualized borrowing rate is 0.02 + 0.10 × utilization, where utilization is debt divided by cash plus debt. Interest accrues against principal plus accrued interest over elapsed time; 10% of booked interest accrues to reserves. Decimal remainder accounting retains sub-ledger fractions. Rates vary with utilization; the formula is not a promised investment return.

POST /api/add-collateral uses loanId and amount in the existing collateral asset. POST /api/repay uses amount in the loan asset, pays interest first, caps payment at debt, and releases proportional collateral. Full repayment sets Repaid. Repayments can release cash to queued Earn redemptions.

The lifecycle worker monitors collateral and can liquidate through the actual spot book. Insufficient counterparties can delay liquidation or leave bad debt; loans and pool claims retain that economic outcome. Inspect loan status, collateral, principal, interest and badDebt rather than assuming collateral always covers debt.

title: Integrated liquidity provision
text:
Integrated liquidity provision

Liquidity providers contribute assets to a shared pool that posts real orders on the exchange's spot, perpetual, expiry-futures and options books. There is no separate AMM instrument or standalone swap venue. Participant orders match AMM quotes through ordinary price-time matching.

 Contribution lifecycle

POST /api/liquidity-deposit accepts BTC, USDT or both. At least one amount must be positive; each supports eight decimal places. Funds move into request escrow. The response is a LiquidityOperation, initially Pending.

The pool seeks approximately equal BTC/USDT value for activation. An imbalanced contribution places spot conversion orders and waits for actual counterparties. It does not fabricate fills or issue shares before conversion completes. Balanced contributions activate at the current net asset value. Existing pool shares make new shares proportional to contributed value; the first deposit establishes initial units.

Track /api/portfolio.liquidityRequests. On Completed, shares appear in liquidity.shares. Fees and trading gains/losses change NAV after activation. Public /api/products.amm reports assets, total shares, feesEarned and marked NAV. Wallet assets alone are not full NAV when the pool has derivative exposure.

 Redemption lifecycle

POST /api/liquidity-withdraw specifies shares and desired BTC/USDT proceeds. Shares already queued cannot be queued again. Pending shares are locked economically but remain in the holding until the request completes.

The pool can redeem a small request without closing every position if it has chosen-asset liquidity and collateral headroom. Otherwise it waits for real fills, collateral release or conversion. Value is calculated at execution; the preview is not a guaranteed payout. Completed requests report received amount and completion time.

POST /api/liquidity-cancel cancels only Pending requests. Withdrawal cancellation unlocks shares. Deposit cancellation returns remaining escrow in its current asset composition; already-executed conversions remain final.

 Quoting and allocation

Spot quotes sample separate segments of a constant-product reserve curve, up to ten levels per side. Derivative quotes use a virtual constant-product inventory curve around reference/option values, bounded by real margin and option coverage. The default target is five levels per side, configurable from one to twenty. Those levels split the existing per-instrument budget; they do not multiply available collateral.

Prices are rounded to ticks and coincident levels are merged. Small pools, insufficient precision, collateral constraints, absent references or post-only crossing checks can produce fewer levels. Quotes never deliberately cross resting orders. Unchanged quotes retain sequence/time priority and receive a freshness revalidation timestamp. Stale AMM quotes cannot execute after their short validity window without revalidation.

LPs receive the configured share of AMM execution fees, currently 80% by default, already included in NAV. Returns also depend on inventory, price movement, derivative exposure and counterparty liquidity. feesEarned is cumulative fee income, not total investment profit. See [fees](./fees.md) for formulas.

Execution fees accrue in their received asset: BTC for spot buys, USDT otherwise. A final all-share USDT redemption returns any BTC remainder smaller than 0.000001 BTC in kind, with a separate balance entry and withdrawal detail. Tradable balances still require actual counterparty conversion.

title: Market data and SignalR
Decimal values and identifiers
text:
Decimal values and identifiers

Amounts, prices, ratios, counters and integer properties are serialized as JSON strings. Booleans remain booleans. Dates are UTC ISO 8601 strings, except candle time, which is Unix seconds encoded as a string. Nullable properties use JSON null; zero is not a substitute for unavailable data.

| Value | Precision / accepted range |
|  |
| Order quantity | Positive BTC, step 0.000001 |
| Limit price | Positive USDT per BTC, tick 0.01 |
| Internal wallet amounts, LP/Earn shares | Up to 8 decimals |
| BTC ERC-20 withdrawal | Up to 8 decimals |
| USDT ERC-20 withdrawal | Up to 6 decimals |
| DCA purchase amount | USDT, up to 6 decimals |
| Average position entry price | Up to 16 decimals |
| Interest/reserve remainder | Up to 20 decimals |
| Leverage | Integer 1–10, JSON string |
| DCA interval | "1", "24" or "168" hours |

Positive validated input amounts are capped at 1,000,000,000. Wallet accounting uses PostgreSQL numeric(28,8) and .NET decimal arithmetic. The browser uses decimal arithmetic for financial calculations; only chart coordinates cross into JavaScript numbers.

Use decimal libraries in integrations. Never apply parseFloat, binary-float multiplication or numeric JSON coercion to balances, order quantities or signatures. Quantize order quantities downward to the allowed step, and choose an intentional price rounding policy. Reject invalid user input instead of silently changing a submitted intent.

python
from decimal import Decimal, ROUND_DOWN
available = Decimal('100.00')
price = Decimal('75000.00')
quantity = (available / (price  Decimal('1.001'))).quantize(
    Decimal('0.000001'), rounding=ROUND_DOWN)
body = {'quantity': format(quantity, 'f'), 'price': format(price, 'f')}


The example reserves a configured-example 0.1% spot fee; read actual deployment fees from /api/config rather than hardcode them.

Instrument IDs identify execution books; symbols label them. Spot ID BTCUSDT and perpetual ID BTC-PERP both display BTCUSDT, with distinct kinds. Expiry and option IDs must be discovered rather than constructed from a presumed naming convention. UUID resource IDs are strings. Sequence and revision strings should be compared using integers with sufficient precision, such as JavaScript BigInt.

title: First integration
text:
First integration

Start with read-only requests against a running local exchange. These commands use a POSIX shell; PowerShell users can run curl.exe with equivalent quoting.

bash
export NOVCIC_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8081
curl -fsS "$NOVCIC_URL/api/health"
curl -fsS "$NOVCIC_URL/api/config"
curl -fsS "$NOVCIC_URL/api/products"
curl -fsS "$NOVCIC_URL/api/market?instrument=BTCUSDT"


Check products.priceFresh, instrument status, and nullable ticker prices. A quiet exchange can have a funded book and no recent executions; lastPrice: null does not mean a price of zero.

 Authenticate

Sign in through the exchange and create a Read key on the API page. Set credentials in your local shell environment, then run the included example:

bash
export NOVCIC_KEY='your-key-uuid'
export NOVCIC_SECRET='your-secret-string'
node examples/signed-request.mjs GET /api/balances
python examples/signed_request.py GET /api/portfolio


Both examples default to the local origin, require explicit credentials, preserve response strings and fail on HTTP errors. They never fund an account or submit an order unless you explicitly pass a POST command.

 Place and reconcile an order

Use a Trade key. Ensure Unified Trading has sufficient funds. Read /api/products for the desired canonical instrument ID and /api/config for tick/step/fee settings. Persist the request UUID and exact JSON payload before sending:

bash
export REQUEST_ID='replace-with-a-new-persisted-uuid'
node examples/signed-request.mjs POST /api/orders \
  '{"instrument":"BTCUSDT","side":"Buy","type":"Limit","quantity":"0.001000","price":"75000.00","leverage":"1","reduceOnly":false}' \
  "$REQUEST_ID"


The price is illustrative; choose an intentional current price. The example is capable of placing a real order on the configured exchange. On an ambiguous response, run the same command with the same UUID. The client creates a fresh nonce and signature automatically.

Read /api/orders for status and /api/trades for executions. A limit order may rest; a market order can partially fill and cancel its remainder. Cancel a remaining order with POST /api/orders/{id}/cancel, body {}, and another persisted command UUID. Reconcile balances and ledger rather than assuming submission success means execution success.

For a JWT workflow, login with a cookie jar, retain the returned access token, and use it in the Authorization header. Session-only operations such as transfers and withdrawals cannot be performed by a Trade key. See the full [authentication guide](./authentication.md).

title: Idempotency and safe retries
text:
Idempotency and safe retries

Financial POSTs require Idempotency-Key, a UUID unique to the account's command intent. Create it before submission and persist it with the method, path and body. The server commits the financial mutation, journal entries, revision update and command receipt atomically under a database transaction lock.

| Result | Client action |
|  |
| 200 with parsed result | Record the result and reconcile the relevant account snapshot |
| 400 domain validation | Correct the rejected intent; use a new key for a changed command |
| 401 authentication failure | Repair credentials; retry the original key and body if the intent is unchanged |
| Timeout, disconnect, 502/503/other 5xx | Outcome is unknown; retry the original key and unchanged body |
| Same key with changed request | Server returns 400; do not reuse keys for different operations |

A repeated committed command returns the saved original response, not a newly calculated account state. An order can fill after that saved response; query orders and executions for its current state.

For HMAC retries, generate a new timestamp, nonce and signature for each HTTP attempt while preserving the idempotency key and JSON body. The signature prevents HTTP replay; the command key prevents duplicate financial effects. They solve different problems.

text
Persist intent + key
  → sign with fresh nonce
  → submit
  → if outcome unknown, submit the same intent/key with another fresh nonce
  → save receipt
  → refresh orders, executions and balances


Command receipts have no configured TTL in this implementation. Do not rely on deleting or recycling keys. Parallel submissions are serialized at the matching authority; clients should bound concurrency and back off on failures rather than flood the server.

Session login/refresh/logout, key creation/revocation and deposit-address creation do not use financial command receipts. Address creation returns the same account address. Key creation can produce another key when repeated, so inspect existing keys after an ambiguous response. toggle-dca does use a receipt: changing its command key on retry could undo the intended pause or resume.

See [authentication](./authentication.md) for signed headers and [errors](./errors.md) for response formats.

title: Cross margin and settlement
text:
Cross margin and settlement

GET /api/portfolio returns risk alongside positions and product holdings. Unified Trading USDT contributes at 100%; unencumbered BTC contributes at 90% of the reference index. Funding wallets are excluded. Option cover is removed from reusable collateral.

Initial margin includes futures positions and open derivative orders. Maintenance margin for futures positions is 0.5% of marked notional. Options are covered: short calls consume BTC and short puts consume full strike-value USDT. Signed realized cash and marked P&L affect equity.

Use transferableUsdt and transferableBtc, not raw wallet availability, for possible outflows. These values are snapshots; the final command rechecks risk atomically. An amount that was transferable a moment ago can be rejected after prices, orders or positions change.

When a required price is stale, priceFresh is false. The index must be at most five seconds old. Option exposure additionally requires usable option references. Risk-increasing actions are blocked; cancellation and Funding-to-Trading collateral top-ups remain available. A restricted account requires attention to maintenance/coverage constraints; the lifecycle worker can cancel orders and attempt liquidation against real counterparties.

 Realized cash

Derivative P&L and option premiums flow through a clearing cash ledger. A positive realizedCash is a claim; it is not permission to mint wallet funds. POST /api/settle-cash settles available funded clearing cash, possibly partially, and leaves the rest pending. A negative claim is an obligation collected from available trading collateral.

Track the returned amount and pending, then refresh balances and portfolio. When no cash needs settlement, the response can contain only message. A profitable position can coexist with an unwithdrawable claim if the other side has not funded settlement.

No endpoint changes margin mode, establishes isolated margin, sets risk tiers or submits a liquidation command for another account. Displaying a slider in a client must not imply capabilities absent from the API.

 Account-wide leverage

portfolio.leverage is the Unified Trading setting for all perpetual and expiry futures. POST /api/leverage accepts an integer string from 1 through 10 and requires an Idempotency-Key. It updates active futures positions and open orders together and rejects changes when margin is insufficient or required pricing is unavailable. Options remain covered; leverage does not reduce their collateral requirements.

POST /api/leverage-preview accepts the same body, checks the proposed account and returns its risk snapshot without committing changes. It requires no idempotency key. Trade HMAC keys and JWT sessions can use both endpoints.

New accounts default to 1?. Migrated accounts use the highest leverage among their active futures positions/orders; this avoids raising margin requirements on migration. The per-order leverage field is deprecated: omit it. A supplied futures value must equal the account setting or the order is rejected.

title: Order lifecycle and products
text:
Order lifecycle and products

The exchange supports spot, perpetual futures, expiry futures and European options on actual separate instrument books. Discover each id, kind, status, expiry and strike through /api/products. The perpetual displays BTCUSDT; its API ID remains BTC-PERP to distinguish it from spot.

 Submit an order

POST /api/orders accepts case-sensitive Buy/Sell and Limit/Market. Quantity is BTC, step 0.000001. Limit price is USDT per BTC, tick 0.01. Use price: null for Market. Orders execute against price-time priority; a resting maker sets the execution price.

| Status | Meaning |
|  |
| Open | No fill yet; remaining quantity rests |
| PartiallyFilled | Some quantity filled; remaining quantity rests |
| Filled | Entire requested quantity filled |
| Cancelled | No further fills; may already have partial executions |

A market order never rests its remainder. Spot rejects an entirely unexecutable market order; derivative market orders can return Cancelled with their entire quantity remaining. A cancellation reason can identify self-trade prevention, unfilled market remainder, stale AMM quote or risk restrictions. Reasons are human-readable strings.

Crossing your own resting order stops execution of the incoming remainder. There are no public batch, amend, stop, trigger, time-in-force or user post-only parameters. Cancel then place a new intent to replace an order; the new order receives new queue priority and can race with fills on the old one.

 Spot

Buy limits reserve quote funds; sells reserve BTC. Fills and wallet/journal movements commit atomically. Integrated AMM orders participate in this same book and matching rules. Every customer fill pays a fee deducted from its received asset. Funding wallets cannot trade directly; transfer to Unified Trading first.

 Perpetual and expiry futures

Contracts settle in USDT under cross margin. Leverage is 1–10. New non-option derivative limit prices must be within 10% of the fresh reference index. Perpetual funding runs at UTC eight-hour boundaries; settlement and funding rely on supported price windows. Expiry futures settle at their discovered expiry, when the required settlement window is available.

reduceOnly: true requires an existing opposite position and quantity no greater than that position. It cannot open a new position. Cancel/fill races can change the remaining position after you read it; inspect the command result and refresh risk.

 Options

Options are European and cash-settled in USDT. Quantity is BTC exposure; price is premium per BTC. Buyers pay premium. Short calls require BTC cover and short puts require strike-value USDT cover. Coverage cannot also be withdrawn or reused for another obligation. Option mark/IV/delta depend on fresh, supported reference inputs; missing values remain null and new risk can pause.

Keep positions, realized cash claims, wallet balances and execution history distinct. A realized profit is not immediately withdrawable unless clearing liquidity has funded it. See [risk](./risk.md) and [fees](./fees.md).

 Affordability, fills and activity

POST /api/order-preview accepts side, type, price (null for Market), instrument, reduceOnly and optional quantity. Set quantity to zero to estimate Max. It returns maximumQuantity, quantity, fee, feeAsset, netReceipt, orderCost, orderCostAsset, revision and error. Order cost is the input asset amount for spot (BTC for sells, USDT for buys) and incremental initial margin plus immediate USDT outflow for derivatives; spot netReceipt accounts for the received-asset fee. Limit estimates include the remaining limit quantity. Market estimates require executable liquidity for the selected quantity.

The preview evaluates the actual engine in rollback-only savepoints under the command lock. It commits no order, balance, trade, receipt or revision. Database identity sequences can have gaps. Debounce preview requests; do not call once per market tick. The snapshot may change before submission. An error field describes an unavailable estimate; maximumQuantity can still identify a smaller affordable quantity. Invalid instruments or unavailable infrastructure may return HTTP errors.

Order responses include filledNotional and averageExecutionPrice. Average is all fill notional divided by executed quantity, including fills outside the recent-trades window; null means no fills. A partially executed market order can be Cancelled with a nonzero average and remaining quantity.

Cancel all applies across the entire account, not just the displayed market. The response cancelled count is authoritative. Balance activity excludes zero-net reserve/release entries before selecting the latest 100; the internal ledger retains them for audit.

title: Contract and design maintenance
text:
Contract and design maintenance

This site is maintained in the independent [novcic/docs repository](https://github.com/novcic/docs), on master. The exchange source lives in the sibling NovcicExchange checkout. Documentation is built with Docusaurus and published through GitHub Actions to GitHub Pages.

 Updating the contract

1. Change and test the exchange behavior. Review public route declarations, authentication rules and response models.
2. Update the audited catalog in NovcicExchange/scripts/export-api.py; run python scripts/sync-docs.py from the exchange.
3. In docs, run node scripts/reference.mjs to regenerate reference/schema pages. Update explanatory guides, examples and this release's changelog where behavior changed.
4. Run npm test and npm run build; inspect the built site on desktop and mobile.
5. Commit the exchange and docs separately on master. Publish the docs commit with the corresponding exchange release.

api/source-manifest.json records SHA-256 hashes of the audited source files. api/openapi.json and static/openapi.json must remain identical. The generated reference must contain one page per operation. CI checks these invariants and builds with broken-link errors enabled. API changes are never considered complete while the contract snapshot is stale.

 Updating branding

NovcicExchange/BRANDING.md and branding/tokens.json define the design contract. Increment the version for intentional design changes, regenerate token CSS, and run the same sync script. Docs has a checked copy of BRANDING.md, token JSON/CSS and the decorative meadow asset. branding/manifest.json records their release hashes; CI rejects accidental divergence.

Keep a single light theme, readable typography, forest-green actions, sage surfaces, aligned decimal values and restrained botanical decoration. Financial examples must preserve exact strings and realistic states. Do not introduce unavailable environments, fake trading activity or unsupported API promises to fill a visual gap.

 Verification

The signing examples have deterministic cross-language vectors. Run a read-only request against a local exchange after protocol changes. Exercise an idempotent order round trip on a dedicated local account after trading changes. Never include private account credentials, cookies, raw signing material or local operational artifacts in this public repository.
